audit.report: The card settlement worker (pid 1660827) became an idle-in-transaction blocker, grinding checkout to 55% success and putting ~$4,748/min of revenue at risk. The Database Guardian recommended a 65s wait, citing the blocker's short runtime and the business's 60s degradation tolerance, while the Continuity Guardian required proof of the protected settlement's ownership and in-flight state before permitting action. After 22s, the blocker cleared itself, checkout recovered to 100% SLO compliance, and all protected operations remained intact.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction settlement worker (pid 1660827) blocked checkout sessions, causing a revenue-at-risk rate of ~$4,748/min until the blocker cleared after 22s.
lessons: For protected_settlement workloads with policy never_interrupt, pre-load the db.protected_settlements and biz.change_calendar evidence before the negotiation starts so the Continuity Guardian can validate ownership and in-flight state in round 1 instead of requesting a revision.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian's wait rationale was sound but required the Continuity Guardian's revision request to surface the missing protected_settlements and change_calendar evidence; the back-and-forth added rounds but ultimately confirmed safety before proceeding.
follow_ups: Add db.protected_settlements and biz.change_calendar to the standard evidence-pack for any workload tagged PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT.
Cache the lock_graph and workload_registry probes at incident start so guardians spend cycles recovering instead of probing.
Validate that the 65s wait budget covers the typical 45s runtime plus a safety margin for protected_settlement batches.
